problem: Prior robot navigation and manipulation systems rely on fixed-category semantic maps and closed-set labels, and cannot follow open-vocabulary, multimodal instructions or handle scalability, long-term object changes, and cross-embodiment generalization.
motivation: Household robots must understand human instructions in dynamic, unstructured environments across diverse tasks. Foundation models (VLMs, LLMs) offer generalizable perception and language comprehension, which the thesis uses to build language-conditioned navigation and manipulation.
key_idea: Use pretrained vision-language foundation models to build open-vocabulary, multimodal, hierarchical 3D semantic maps and scene-specific object memory for navigation, and contribute to unified cross-embodiment data and a VLA model for manipulation.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims that per-pixel visual-language features let natural-language queries highlight regions dynamically, that a hierarchical 3D scene graph cuts map size by 75% while keeping semantic richness, and that combining foundation-model features with a scene-specific point cloud encoder gives near-perfect object association.
method: Open-vocabulary spatial-goal semantic map (VLMaps): fuses per-pixel VLM visual-language features into a map so language queries highlight regions, supporting goals like 'middle of the chair and the sofa'
LLM API-call generation: LLMs turn human instructions into API calls for complex spatial goal specification
Multimodal semantic map (AVLMaps): integrates visual, language and audio features, so goals can be given as text, images or sounds
Hierarchical open-vocabulary 3D scene graph (HOV-SG): reduces map size by 75% and lets quadruped robots navigate multi-story buildings with language
Scene-specific point cloud encoder + object memory bank: object association over long-term dynamics, combined with foundation-model features, to recognize relocated objects
Open-X-Embodiment / VLA: unifies global manipulation datasets and trains a vision-language-action model for zero-shot deployment across robot embodiments

setting.backbone: Pretrained VLMs/LLMs for maps (mostly frozen), a scene-specific point cloud encoder, and a VLA model (RT-X style)
setting.training_data: Not detailed in the abstract; Open-X-Embodiment multi-robot manipulation datasets for the VLA
setting.observation: RGB-D, audio, point clouds (details not given)
setting.simulator: not specified; tested in real-world settings

results: The abstract reports a 75% map size reduction with the hierarchical 3D scene graph and near-perfect object association accuracy with the scene-specific encoder. It also reports real-world tests on multiple robot platforms and multi-story traversal, but gives no benchmark numbers or baselines.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so no quantitative benchmark comparisons could be extracted
Evaluation appears to be mostly real-world or custom setups, which makes comparison with standard benchmarks difficult
